turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mr. Hale, thanks for hanging in. I saw you circling the lot, it's a zoo out there today. What brings you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, it's this cough. Started after I had the flu, and it's been six weeks, give or take. I don't know, doctor, it just won't let up.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Six weeks, starting right after the flu. Is it dry, or are you bringing mucus up?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly dry. There's a little clear stuff in the morning, not yellow. Nights are awful, I'm up at two, sometimes three, hacking.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Wakes you at night. Any fever or chills with it?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I checked a few times. Thermometer's old, but it wasn't high.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): No fever on those checks. Any blood in what you cough up?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. I'd have come in faster.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Understood. Chest pain? Short of breath?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. Well, the muscles across my chest get sore from coughing, that's different. Stairs wind me a little, but that's been for years, not from this.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest wall sore from the cough, and the stair shortness is longstanding. Have you lost weight?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't think so. I still clean my plate.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright. Any travel lately, even a long drive out of town?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. We were gonna see my brother in Ohio, then the alternator went, so we sat at home. I don't mind, that highway wears me out.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): So no travel. Have you been around anyone with tuberculosis, or a cough being treated as TB?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't know anyone with TB.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): There was an x-ray mentioned in an old note. Do you remember what they said?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Urgent care. They said it was borderline. I don't know, doctor, I kind of nodded and never went back.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Called borderline. When was that film?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Maybe two years ago. Could've been last spring. I really don't know.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): So a prior chest x-ray, reported to you as borderline, and the date isn't clear. What have you used for the cough?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, benzonatate. The pearls, a hundred milligrams. I stopped it in March, my mouth went numb and I was done.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stopped the benzonatate in March. Did anyone prescribe prednisone around the flu?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): They sent it to the pharmacy and I never picked it up. I don't like steroids. My neighbor takes them for everything, not me.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): You never started the prednisone. What do you take regularly?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Lisinopril, ten milligrams, every morning, for my blood pressure. Years.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Lisinopril 10 milligrams each morning for blood pressure, ongoing. Any allergies to medications?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): No medication allergies. Do you smoke, or did you?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I quit, um, about ten years ago. It was around a pack a day. My wife still gives me the look if I stand near the smokers outside the grocery store.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Former smoker, stopped about ten years ago, about a pack a day before that. Deep breath in, and out. Lungs are clear, no wheeze and no crackles.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Huh. Guy at the tire shop said clear lungs means you're fine. He also thinks motor oil fixes arthritis, so.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't lean on that. With a cough going six weeks, I was going to start azithromycin for five days and see you back in two weeks.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, if you say so. I don't know, doctor. Wait, though, my sister called the other day.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Go ahead.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): She said our cousin Dale was in the hospital in Arizona. She thinks it was TB, or maybe pneumonia, she wasn't sure. I never went out there. I didn't see him.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me play that back. No travel, you did not visit Dale, and your sister thinks he was hospitalized for tuberculosis or pneumonia, which one you can't confirm.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. That's the whole story. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Earlier you said no weight loss. Clothes fitting the same? Belt?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, no, the pants are loose. I cinched the belt a notch, maybe two. I said no 'cause there's no scale in the house. I don't know how many pounds.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Clothes looser, amount not measured. I'm changing the plan. I am not going to start azithromycin today.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): So no antibiotic? I already talked myself into it.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): No antibiotic today. I'm also not going to put a name on the cause sitting here. A chest x-ray is what I want next.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Can I do that today? The afternoon's kind of open, except I told my wife I'd grab milk.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll order it now. If radiology has a slot this afternoon, go down; otherwise they'll schedule you this week. It will get done.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): And I see you after?

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. Follow up with me once the film is back, about a week. If you cough up blood, get a fever, or your breathing turns sharply worse, don't sit on it, call or go to urgent care.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Should I restart the benzonatate so I can sleep?
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leave it stopped. It numbed your mouth and it won't sort this out. Keep taking the lisinopril the way you have been.

spec.situation: Cough for six weeks after flu; worse at night; patient says no weight loss, then says clothes are loose; recent travel or TB contact denied by patient but a family member recalls a cousin's illness; doctor orders chest X-ray, avoids naming a cause.
features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

omissions.text: Cough wakes him at night, up at 2–3 AM hacking.
The patient denied chills when asked about fever or chills.
Shortness of breath on stairs is longstanding and not from this current cough.
Initial denial of weight loss was corrected: he later reported looser clothes and belt tightened by 1–2 notches, with no home scale to quantify pounds lost.
The patient denied known tuberculosis exposure initially.

He later disclosed only a possible indirect TB exposure: sister said cousin Dale in Arizona was hospitalized for TB or maybe pneumonia, but patient did not travel there or see him, and diagnosis was unconfirmed.
Benzonatate was stopped in March because it caused mouth numbness.
Prednisone had been prescribed around the flu but the patient never picked it up and never started it.

The doctor initially planned azithromycin for 5 days and follow-up in 2 weeks, but after the weight-loss history changed, the plan was changed: no azithromycin and no diagnostic label assigned at the visit.
